subject.title: RFC 0010 (draft): Analyst-skill seams on a pipeline-shaped session substrate

question: Should OpenClaw standardize Gateway-owned raw/processed/curated session seams for opt-in policy analysis, or keep this capability outside the core session substrate?
rationale: The RFC deliberately introduces a privileged control-plane data path, new per-claw governance configuration, and a long-lived storage/skill contract; benchmarks can inform the choice but cannot establish maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed RFC
options.body: Keep the RFC open and require a compatibility map to the merged storage RFC plus an explicit analyst-skill trust, evidence-integrity, and opt-in upgrade model before acceptance.

options.title: Prefer plugin experimentation
options.body: Defer a core substrate contract and ask for a plugin or prototype that demonstrates which currently missing generic extension seams are actually required.

options.title: Reject the substrate direction
options.body: Retain the current session model and close the RFC if maintainers do not want policy analysis embedded in the Gateway-owned persistence path.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed RFC
recommendation.body: Keep the RFC open and require a compatibility map to the merged storage RFC plus an explicit analyst-skill trust, evidence-integrity, and opt-in upgrade model before acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged session/transcript storage RFC is the closest accepted contract that this decision would extend or constrain.
